categories.description: A prospective client describing work they want built or automated. Includes anyone asking about price, scope or availability for new work.
An existing client reporting that something already delivered has broken, stopped or needs changing.
Unsolicited bulk outreach selling a service, lead generation, SEO or marketing. Not a genuine enquiry about the recipient's services.
A recruiter or employer offering a permanent or contract job rather than buying a service.

options.systemPromptTemplate: Classify the enquiry by what the sender wants from the recipient. Judge intent, not tone or politeness — a well-written sales pitch is still a sales pitch, and a blunt one-line message from an existing client is still support.

attributes.name: contact_name
attributes.description: The sender's name as signed off. Empty string if not given.

attributes.name: organisation
attributes.description: The company or organisation the sender represents. Empty string if not stated.

attributes.name: problem_summary
attributes.description: One sentence, in plain English, describing the operational problem they want solved.

attributes.name: systems_mentioned
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of named software, tools or platforms mentioned. Empty string if none.

attributes.name: budget_stated
attributes.description: The budget figure in GBP if one is given. Use the lower end of any range. Return 0 if no budget is mentioned.

attributes.name: deadline_mentioned
attributes.description: Any date or timeframe the sender needs the work by, exactly as written. Empty string if none.

attributes.name: manual_hours_claimed
attributes.description: Hours per week of manual work the sender says the problem costs them. Return 0 if not stated.

options.systemPromptTemplate: Extract only what the sender actually wrote. Never infer a budget, a deadline or an hour count that is not stated — a wrong number here leads to a wrong quote.

assignments.name: queue
assignments.value: recruitment — no action unless actively looking

parameters.content:
## 1. Intake

Samples inline so the workflow runs with only a model credential.

In production this is a Webhook from the contact form, or a Gmail trigger on the inbox.

## 2. Classify by intent

Five outputs. Only genuine new business goes down the expensive path — the other four are handled cheaply and never reach the model again.

Judging intent rather than tone is what stops a polite sales pitch being treated as a lead.

## 3. Extract, then score in code

The model extracts only what was written — it is explicitly forbidden from inventing a budget or a deadline.

Ranking then happens in plain JavaScript, not in a prompt: auditable, adjustable by the client, and identical every run. It also lists what is still unknown, so nothing gets quoted blind.

## 4. Draft — never send

A reply is drafted and queued for a human. Nothing is sent automatically, and the prompt forbids claiming experience or quoting a price.

That boundary is deliberate. Auto-replying to prospects is how automation loses a client its reputation.
